name: jobsite-safety-reference
description: Construction-safety answers in ChatGPT: verbatim OSHA rule text with citations, OSHA recordability checks, and nearly 300 toolbox talks in English and Spanish. No account needed.

interface.longDescription:
Ask ChatGPT what an OSHA standard actually says, and get the regulation text itself with its citation: 29 CFR plus the California, Washington and Oregon heat and wildfire-smoke rules, OSHA interpretations and NIOSH/CDC/EPA guidance, each labeled binding law or guidance. Describe an injury and Jobsite applies the OSHA 1904 recordability rules, cites the rule text, and gives any report-to-OSHA deadline, or asks for the facts it still needs. Get a ready-to-deliver toolbox talk on any construction hazard, in English or Spanish, from Jobsite's library of nearly 300. Also: recent OSHA rulemaking and news, and how Jobsite works.

No sign-in and no company data. ChatGPT can also start a sample Jobsite workspace you can claim and explore. To run talks with your crew and keep the sign-in record, track training and certifications, or keep your OSHA log, connect the Jobsite plugin instead. Docs: jobsitecerts.com/mcp.
defaultPrompt: What does 29 CFR 1926.501 require for fall protection on a residential roof?
Give me a 10-minute toolbox talk on trench cave-ins, in Spanish.
A worker got a tetanus shot after a nail puncture and went back to work. Is that recordable?
